arXiv:2608.17162v1 [cs.LG] 17 Aug 2026

OraclePhys: A Systematic Framework for
LLM Fine-Tuning on Structural Mechanics

Mingyu Li Affiliation: University of Houston    Guorui Song Affiliation: Tsinghua University Correspondence:mli52@cougarnet.uh.edu    Jing Lin Affiliation: Tsinghua University Correspondence:mli52@cougarnet.uh.edu    Haoqian Wang Affiliation: Tsinghua University Correspondence:mli52@cougarnet.uh.edu
Abstract

What a language model internalizes from fine-tuning is usually diagnosed after the fact. We make it an experimental variable. OraclePhys is a systematic fine-tuning framework with three components: OraclePhys-Bench, an exactly-graded structural-mechanics benchmark whose finite-element oracle scores every answer and counterfactual edit—no human labels, no LLM judging; OraclePhys-30K, a supervision dataset of seven answer forms over byte-identical structure descriptions; and a controlled training study across the seven forms and three verifier roles. The study yields two findings. First, the label’s answer form—not its bit count—causally determines what fine-tuning teaches: a ranking objective installs an out-of-distribution forward model where the untrained base sits at the guessing prior, a scalar objective at best a partial one, a boolean nothing detectable; the vector–scalar gulf survives a second physics domain, a second model family, and a paraphrased evaluation surface. Second, written or score-filtered answers install this capability, while advantage-weighted scores (GRPO) raise reward yet leave the model statistically equivalent to its start on held-out physics—within the recipes and budgets tested—sufficing only for routing. The trained 8B—the first LLM on spatial structural response—reaches the task’s data-precision frontier: above a frontier LLM at zero- and 32-shot, at a specialist’s level. What the label spells out about the target computation is what fine-tuning teaches; what you train on is what you route.

1 Introduction

Training objectives are usually chosen for gradeability: a scalar loss, a pass/fail check, a preference score. What a language model internalizes under a given objective is diagnosed only after the fact, by probing or benchmarking—a literature of striking negative results (Vafa et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024) that observes but does not intervene. Whether the objective itself causally determines what is internalized, everything else held fixed, has not been isolated as an experimental variable.

We isolate it with OraclePhys-Bench (§2): a finite-element solver returns the exact per-story lateral response of any steel frame; the spatial target is non-local in the input text, and intervention probes have verified answers.

The testbed is a model organism for a question about training, not a benchmark of engineering practice. Whether the label’s answer form determines what fine-tuning teaches is live well beyond this domain (Kung and Peng, 2023; Webson and Pavlick, 2022; Zhou et al., 2023). Deciding between such readings requires byte-identical inputs, labels with controlled information content, and a grader that scores every counterfactual—properties no natural corpus offers and this domain provides by construction (Li et al., 2023). The price—a single training template—is stated in Limitations; the purchase: every contrast is controlled, not correlational.

The experiment trains on OraclePhys-30K, holding the base model, training structures, and input text byte-identical and varying only the answer form the objective demands: full per-story ranking (P), peak scalar (A), or pass/fail boolean (O). The ranking objective installs a forward model (0.86–0.91 OOD localization vs. 0.19–0.25 untrained), the scalar at best a partial one, the boolean nothing detectable (§3); the vector–scalar gulf replicates on a second physics domain, a second model family, and a paraphrased evaluation surface.

The same oracle then dissociates the ways a verifier can enter training (§4–5): written or score-filtered answers install; advantage-weighted scores leave the model statistically equivalent to its start while reward climbs—yet suffice to wire a −0.15-0.15 action-interface gap shut; an explicit reasoning channel adds nothing but an installation cost.

Ceiling analyses (§6) locate these results: a frontier model sits near a 30-line formula, a specialist GNN matches the trained 8B, and six learners converge on a band set by the precision of the data, not by task difficulty.

Contributions.

  • •

    We build OraclePhys-Bench, an exactly-graded testbed for structural mechanics, with verified surface-cue removal, intervention probes, and an isomorphic second domain—a controlled instrument, not a leaderboard.

  • •

    We release OraclePhys-30K, a supervision dataset of seven answer forms over byte-identical structure descriptions.

  • •

    We present the first LLM trained on per-story structural response (prior systems wrap solvers or treat scalar beam statics; §7), via a controlled study—seven supervision forms, three verifier roles, one exact oracle—training an 8B to the task’s data-precision frontier: above Claude Opus 4.8 at zero- and 32-shot, at a specialist GNN’s level.

  • •

    We establish two findings: the answer form of the supervision label, not its bit count, determines what fine-tuning teaches; and, within the recipes tested, written or score-filtered answers teach what advantage-weighted scores do not—scores suffice for routing, not for installation.

2 An Oracle-Graded Testbed for Spatial Forward Models

2.1 Task and oracle

The subject domain is the lateral response of 2-D steel frames (Fig. 1): multi-story, multi-bay, with per-story sections, a connection type, optional braces, damage events, and a lateral load whose vertical profile varies. An OpenSees finite-element model returns, for any structure, the per-story inter-story drift ratios

δk=uk−uk−1hk,k∗=arg⁡maxk⁡δk,\delta_{k}\;=\;\frac{u_{k}-u_{k-1}}{h_{k}},\qquad k^{*}\;=\;\arg\max_{k}\,\delta_{k}, (1)

where uku_{k} is the lateral displacement of floor kk (u0=0u_{0}{=}0 at the base) and hkh_{k} the story height; the governing story k∗k^{*} is the story that governs the design. Soft or damaged stories drift more, and a brace stiffens its story. The FE solution defines ground truth for this task, and grading against it is deterministic and exact, so no human annotation and no model-based judging appear anywhere in training or evaluation.

The model sees only a natural-language description (geometry, per-story sections, connections, braces, damage, load) and must rank all stories by drift, in JSON. Primary metrics: top-1 localization of the governing story and Spearman ρ\rho of the full ranking, on held-out structures (n=150n{=}150 per axis; 80 for extrapolation).

Two properties make this testbed diagnostic rather than merely hard: structural weakness is spatially non-local (no single sentence of the description reveals the governing story), and every claimed capability can be probed by intervention—the oracle grades counterfactuals, so “strengthen a story; where does weakness move?” has a verified answer. Throughout the paper, “installs a forward model” (our operationalization of a world model in this domain) is a behavioral claim—performance on the intervention-probing axes of §2.2—not a claim about internal representations. Not for lack of trying: linear probes decode the governing story equally from every arm—including the behaviorally inert O—at a surface-level baseline; probe-based measurement is insensitive to a two-to-sixfold behavioral difference here (Limitations).

2.2 Evaluation axes

All axes use deterministic instance streams (§2.4) and the same parser; a parse failure scores as a miss.

Forward localization / ranking: rank the stories of an unseen structure (OOD structures have 5–6 stories vs. 3–4 in training, so every test ranking is longer than any seen in training). Post-intervention forward: the governing story is strengthened; localize the new one from the edited description—anti-correlated with the pre-edit answer by construction (post-edit family present in training; Limitations). Two-step horizon: two sequential edits—errors compound. Extrapolation: forward localization on the tallest structures. Action interface: the original structure plus a one-sentence action (“add a brace to story 3”), applied internally; a paired control rewrites the same transition as a full post-edit description, so the act−-desc gap isolates action-application (§5). Invariance (sanity): strengthening a story must not make it relatively weaker.

2.3 Two difficulty tiers, and killing the surface

Tier-1 (realistic) structures follow design practice, leaving exploitable regularities; tier-2 (hardened) randomizes them (section jitter, composed weakening, varied load shapes). Hardening is verified: a bag-of-words probe falls 0.63→0.260.63\to 0.26 (chance 0.18), the structured-feature probe from 0.76 to 0.57, a geometry-only probe staying near tier-1 (Appendix B)—no lexical shortcut that clears the first-order formula survives.

The non-learning reference is a 30-line first-order formula (story shear over a stiffness proxy). It is biased against us—it reads numeric section properties directly from the design object—and its tier-2 scores (0.45/0.47) sit well above random: any physics claim must clear this row.

2.4 Splits, determinism, and statistics

Training structures have 3–4 stories; the OOD pool has 5–6 under held-out geometry. All streams generate deterministically from fixed seeds: every run—across models, checkpoints, months—answers the same 150 questions per axis. This buys three things. (i) Bit-exact reproducibility under greedy decoding and fixed batching. (ii) Paired statistics: per-instance correctness arrays are stored in every results file, and all model comparisons are exact McNemar tests (McNemar, 1947) on discordant pairs with paired bootstrap CIs. This paper reports ∼50{\sim}50 paired tests; the staircase claims rest on p<10−4p<10^{-4} effects that survive any standard multiplicity correction; the answers-vs-scores dissociation rests on installation effects at p≤0.005p\leq 0.005 and on powered direct endpoint contrasts on fresh n=600n{=}600 streams (n=1800n{=}1800 pooled over disjoint axes, p<10−12p<10^{-12}; Table 8); and we treat p∈[0.01,0.05]p\in[0.01,0.05] results that do not survive the Table 5 FDR as secondary, corroborating evidence. (iii) Machine-checkable provenance: one script regenerates every number from archived per-instance files, pairing fingerprint-checked; the exported streams, grader, and reference rows constitute OraclePhys-Bench, and fresh streams mint on demand as a contamination defense.

3 The Objective-Shape Staircase

3.1 One knob: how much of the answer the objective carries

Three training arms share the base model (Qwen3-8B + LoRA), update budget, ∼4{\sim}4k training structures, and byte-identical input text (asserted at build time with a token-level leakage audit), differing only in the question-and-answer suffix. With 𝜹\boldsymbol{\delta} from Eq. 1 and drift limit τ\tau, the three labels are

yP\displaystyle y_{\mathrm{P}} =argsort↓𝜹,yA=maxkδk,\displaystyle=\operatorname{argsort}_{\downarrow}\,\boldsymbol{\delta},\qquad y_{\mathrm{A}}=\max_{k}\delta_{k}, (2)
yO\displaystyle y_{\mathrm{O}} =[maxkδk≤τ],\displaystyle=\mathbf{1}\!\left[\max_{k}\delta_{k}\leq\tau\right],

carrying, for an nsn_{s}-story structure, ∼log2⁡(ns!)≈2.6{\sim}\log_{2}(n_{s}!)\approx 2.6–4.64.6 bits (P, ranking), ∼1{\sim}1–22 useful bits (A, scalar; no story named, though the scalar is a function of the argmax), and ≤1{\leq}1 bit (O, boolean compliance). Arm A is not a straw man: it models the aggregate-right, localization-wrong failure mode this testbed is built to detect; its calibrated scores confirm real (if partial) structure (§3.3). The knob is not task difficulty but how much of the oracle’s spatial answer the objective exposes. Across the seven answer-form arms (∼3.8{\sim}3.8k rows each over the same structures), the hardened second-round curriculum, and the action-interface pairs, OraclePhys-30K totals ∼30{\sim}30K oracle-graded examples (glossary and composition: Appendix C).

3.2 The vector–scalar gulf, three times

Fig. 2 shows OOD governing-story localization across frames/Qwen (3 seeds), heat/Qwen, and frames/Llama: P reaches 0.86–0.91 in all three settings, while A and O separate cleanly from base only in the primary one (heat: O 0.33 ≈\approx A 0.29, both near base; O not run on Llama; full tables in Appendix F). The gulf replicates on a second physics domain—2-D steady-state heat conduction, a structural isomorph (rows ↔\leftrightarrow stories, cooling ↔\leftrightarrow braces) with its own surface-cue audit—and on a second model family with the same data and recipe. The scalar arm’s partial emergence is the exception, not the rule (0.56 on frames/Qwen; heat 0.29 raw; Llama at base under calibration, cf. 0.11 raw); the vector–scalar gulf is the invariant, and the full ordering holds in the primary setting under paired tests (§3.3). The two domains share no exploitable surface: the frames-trained P arm transferred zero-shot to heat collapses to chance-level localization (0.133 vs. 0.187 uniform over heat rankings; the heat population prior is 0.25) while its output format survives intact—each installation is domain-specific.

3.3 Format-calibrated control: knowledge, not output format

A and O never produced a ranking in training, so the raw staircase conflates missing knowledge with format failure—flagged by two below-base anomalies, the signature of a measurement artifact. We therefore re-ran every arm with two worked examples prepended (fmt2; the tier-1 stream throughout §3.3–3.4): identical prompt for every arm, equalizing format while adding minimal task information (base 0.25→0.300.25\to 0.30; cf. Min et al., 2022).

Under calibration the staircase stands: P 0.73≫0.73\gg A 0.47≫0.47\gg O 0.33≈0.33\approx base 0.300.30 (P>>A +0.27+0.27/+0.29+0.29 fwd/post-int, A>>base +0.17+0.17/+0.26+0.26, all p<10−4p<10^{-4}; O−-base n.s.). Both anomalies disappear, as the artifact hypothesis predicts (Qwen-O rises to base; calibrated Llama-A no longer trails its base). On Llama the scalar arm installs nothing measurable while the vector–scalar gulf is 92:3 discordant (p<10−4p<10^{-4}, Table 6)—more absolute than on Qwen. The cleaned reading is sharper than the raw one: the ranking objective installs the full spatial ordering, the scalar objective installs a real but partial one, and the boolean objective installs nothing detectable—what the label spells out about the spatial answer, in directly usable form, is what fine-tuning teaches (§3.4 shows the currency is the spelled-out answer, not its bit count). Calibrated A, at 0.47, stays below the formula’s 0.53: partial installation is weak, and it is the staircase’s one setting-dependent rung (heat 0.29 raw; Llama at base calibrated). P itself dips to 0.733 under prepended examples, which are off-distribution for an SFT’d model; both regimes are reported, and the P ≫\gg A ≫\gg O ordering is invariant in each.

The gate survives a second linguistic surface.

Re-rendering the held-out instances through a paraphrased template (running prose, reordered fields, reworded phrasings; identical information, question, and parser) and re-evaluating the frozen checkpoints leaves the gate unchanged: raw P 0.847 vs. its own checkpoint’s 0.887 (3-seed mean 0.86), and calibrated ladder 0.75/0.44/0.31/0.29 vs. the original 0.73/0.47/0.33/0.30 (Table 9). What the ranking objective installs is readable from a surface it was never trained on; the scalar arm is the more surface-sensitive (raw 0.35).

3.4 Controls: format, task proximity, bit count

Does the staircase measure the label’s information, or merely the proximity between training task and evaluation? Four further arms, all on byte-identical structure text, dissociate the candidates. K keeps A’s scalar format but changes the content: each example asks for the drift of one randomly designated story ({"story_drift": 0.0041}), exposing the per-story field pointwise—never a ranking. V asks for the full drift-value vector—an information superset of the ranking, since values determine order. G asks only which story governs (∼log2⁡ns≈2{\sim}\log_{2}n_{s}\approx 2 bits). S is the placebo: P’s question and answer format verbatim, with content-free shuffled permutations as labels—a training-side control task in the sense of Hewitt and Liang (2019).

The suite orders as: base 0.30 ≈\approx S 0.35 << A 0.47 << K 0.61 == V 0.61 << G 0.68 ≲\lesssim P 0.73 (calibrated localization; key tests: K>>A p=10−4p{=}10^{-4}, V==K p=1.0p{=}1.0, V<<P p=0.011p{=}0.011, G vs. P p=0.27p{=}0.27; Table 5). Three readings. Format installs nothing: the placebo stays at base (and degrades intervention behavior, −0.06-0.06); K, which never produced a ranking, recovers over half the gulf under calibration (raw K==A), bounding task proximity at +0.13+0.13 in that regime. (Control-suite arms are single runs, read against the gate arms’ seed spread; see Limitations.) Bit count alone does not explain it: against the expectation pre-stated in the released builder, the value vector—an information superset of the ranking—lands on the pointwise arm (p=1.0p{=}1.0) and below P: value content plausibly installs a magnitude-reading model whose derived orderings pay the precision toll of §6—a hypothesis our ordinal probes cannot test; the value-readout axis (Limitations) would decide it. Supervision mass fails the same test: the shortest label (G) lands highest among controls, the longest (V) does not. Two pincers close on one conclusion—on the amount axis, minimal G matches P while superset V does not; on the operation axis (calibrated), value arms lead A on forward reading while A leads them post-intervention—each killing one monotone story. The answer itself does: two bits naming the governing story buy 0.68 localization, not distinguishable from P at our single-run resolution (p=0.27p{=}0.27; G trails on full-ranking ρ\rho, 0.72 vs. 0.86). The content-type dissociation also appears post-intervention under calibration: V trails A (−0.107-0.107, p=0.011p{=}0.011, q=0.04q{=}0.04) despite leading on localization—scoped to that regime (the raw rows order differently, and no parse-level data yet separates format from knowledge there; the main staircase is invariant across both). Across the suite, what installs tracks what the label spells out—format and bit count closed, task proximity bounded.

What emerges without being trained.

Training contains single-structure ranking questions only, yet the P arm acquires two-step rollout (0.72), taller-structure generalization (extrapolation 0.82±0.020.82{\pm}0.02 from 3–4-story supervision), and post-intervention localization (0.71, anti-correlated with pattern replay by construction); on heat the same untrained axes emerge (0.82/0.73); A, with identical data and compute, acquires them only attenuated (0.42 calibrated). Two-step and extrapolation cannot be answered by replaying training statistics (post-intervention caveat: Limitations): the ranking objective forced a computation extending to questions training never asked—what the dense objective buys is precisely the transferable part.

4 One Oracle, Two Uses: Answers Install; Advantage-Weighted Scores Do Not

Design.

The oracle enters training in three roles—teacher, filter, judge—collapsing into two uses: answers versus scores. From the same start (the tier-1 P arm, 0.660 tier-2) on the same hardened pool, the teacher protocol trains on oracle-written rankings (dense SFT); the judge optimizes oracle scores of sampled rankings (GRPO; budgets in Appendix C). Weights, LoRA configuration, and prompts are shared: the variable is how the oracle’s knowledge enters the gradient (Fig. 3).

Results.

The teacher protocol gains +0.09+0.09 to +0.14+0.14 across axes (Table 1, Appendix D; seed 42; 3 seeds: forward 0.731±0.0110.731\pm 0.011 from 0.660, post-intervention 0.691±0.0080.691\pm 0.008, the latter individually significant in every seed, p≤0.0013p\leq 0.0013) with essentially no tier-1 forgetting (0.887→0.8670.887\to 0.867). (Convention: paired rows cite the canonical seed-42 checkpoint, 0.747 forward; seed means are reported wherever 3 seeds exist.) The judge protocol leaves the forward, extrapolation, and two-step axes within noise (Tables 5, 6; the one post-intervention cell is flagged below)—while its own reward climbs 0.80 to 0.93: margins sharpen on already-solved instances, which the reward registers and accuracy does not. Powered direct contrasts settle the endpoint comparison: pooling the three disjoint OOD axes on fresh n=600n{=}600 streams, the dense endpoint leads GRPO round-2 by +0.087+0.087 (p=1.7×10−14p{=}1.7\times 10^{-14}) and the headroom run by +0.105+0.105 (p=4×10−18p{=}4\times 10^{-18}), RFT leads GRPO by +0.081+0.081 (p<10−13p{<}10^{-13}), and the judge’s endpoint is TOST-equivalent to its own start (±0.05\pm 0.05, n=1800n{=}1800; Table 8).

Three further cells complete the picture. RL on the strongest base: GRPO continued from the dense-SFT checkpoint under a matched oracle-call budget lands at 0.760 vs. 0.747 (Δ=+0.01\Delta=+0.01, p=0.81p=0.81): once the knowledge is installed, scores have nothing detectable left to add. RL from scratch: GRPO from the untrained base raises its reward 0.20→0.450.20\to 0.45 yet localizes at 0.433 on tier-1—below the formula’s 0.533—and at random (0.167) on the hardened tier: format compliance plus population-prior guessing, the prior-amplification signature of spurious-reward RLVR (Shao et al., 2025). The one candidate RL installation gain sits on one axis: GRPO from the P arm lifts post-intervention (tier-2 +0.080+0.080, p=0.023p{=}0.023, the one judge cell past 0.05; fails FDR, q=0.060q{=}0.060, Table 5)—margin sharpening on the axis §5 shows scores route. We flagged it rather than fold it into either reading; on the fresh n=600n{=}600 stream it dissolves (+0.017+0.017, p=0.35p{=}0.35): the judge-side null is uniform at higher power.

Provenance, recipe, and headroom controls.

Filtered self-distillation (the STaR/RAFT/ReST recipe, used here as a measurement; Zelikman et al., 2022; Dong et al., 2023; Gulcehre et al., 2023; Singh et al., 2024): sample 50 per hardened prompt from the P checkpoint, oracle-score, keep the best with reward ≥0.9\geq 0.9 (93% coverage), imitate the survivors—the oracle contributes nothing but scores, yet the gradient is dense imitation. This installs (+0.093+0.093 forward, +0.127+0.127 post-intervention; p≤0.005p{\leq}0.005, Tables 3, 5), indistinguishably from oracle-written labels (one cost: tier-1 retention 0.820 vs. 0.867). This cell doubles as the pool-adequacy control: the sampled pool demonstrably contains transferable signal—a dense update extracts it; group-relative advantages did not. Best-practice GRPO—group size 50, a difficulty-filtered pool, the strongest SFT base, ∼10×{\sim}10\times the dense round’s oracle-call budget—lands at +0.033+0.033 on its first seed (p=0.18p{=}0.18); across three seeds, 0.751±0.0300.751\pm 0.030 against the 0.747 start, a mean gain of +0.004+0.004. Headroom-matched GRPO—the identical recipe from the pre-hardening 0.660 start, whose runway (+0.12+0.12 across the four axes) the dense round itself consumed—moves +0.013+0.013 (p=0.81p{=}0.81; three seeds 0.678±0.0140.678\pm 0.014 from 0.660; in-pool localization 0.41→0.550.41\to 0.55; Fig. 8). Update-scale probe: dense SFT trains at ∼100×{\sim}100\times GRPO’s learning rate with multi-epoch reuse (budgets in Appendix C), so we re-ran best-practice GRPO at tenfold lr (10−510^{-5}): it does not unlock installation but erodes it (forward 0.747→0.6800.747\to 0.680; four-axis pooled −0.074-0.074, p=8×10−4p{=}8\times 10^{-4}, Table 6)—within this window, the null does not reverse with update magnitude. (In-pool comparisons exist, Xiong et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2025; ours add the held-out outcome and an oracle-label control.) The same sampled tail, selected by the same verifier, transferred under dense imitation and did not under group-relative advantages; why consolidation transfers under one update and not the other we leave open (candidates: token-level credit assignment, multi-epoch reuse of survivors, the KL-conservatism of on-policy updates, Shenfeld et al., 2025).

Alternative explanations.

Five rival readings—reward sparsity, optimizer failure, exploration, headroom, capacity—fail against dedicated cells (Appendix D); most pointedly, endpoints track starting points (0.678±0.0140.678\pm 0.014 from 0.660, where oracle labels reach 0.747), and the same LoRA rank accepts the knowledge whenever the oracle writes or filters it.

Mechanism: what a score can and cannot carry.

Decomposing per-instance behavior explains the asymmetry. With rewards r1:gr_{1:g} over a group of gg samples, each completion’s advantage is

A^i=ri−1g​∑j=1grj:\hat{A}_{i}\;=\;r_{i}\;-\;\tfrac{1}{g}\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{g}r_{j}: (3)

group-relative RL redistributes probability among behaviors the policy already samples—selecting the better half on swing instances, sharpening margins on stable-correct ones—while on stable-wrong instances, precisely those embodying missing knowledge, the rewards nearly coincide, A^i≈0\hat{A}_{i}\approx 0 (Eq. 3), and no gradient points toward the absent computation. The decomposition is measured, not assumed: 50 samples per hardened prompt give ∼60%/34%/6%{\sim}60\%/34\%/6\% (stable-correct/swing/stable-wrong), the stable-wrong reward spread (0.050) matching the training-time collapse endpoint (0.122→0.0490.122\to 0.049); and the tail is shallow (pass@1 0.796, pass@50 0.941), so g=50g{=}50 unlocks gradient on only 2.8% more prompts—why the best-practice cell buys nothing more. What this account does not explain is the transfer asymmetry itself: in-pool localization rises 0.74→0.880.74\to 0.88, yet the OOD axes stand still while imitating the same samples moves them; we report the asymmetry as the finding, mechanism open.

A group-relative comparison orders behaviors the policy already produces; a dense label specifies the full answer with token-level credit. The reward is also underdetermined—format-plus-prior policies score like physics-reading ones in-distribution (the from-scratch cell)—while the exact hardened ranking cannot be produced cheaply (§2.3).

Scope. These are results for one task family, one algorithm (GRPO), one scale (8B+LoRA), ≤\leq800 steps, lr 10−610^{-6}–10−510^{-5}; prolonged-RL regimes (Liu et al., 2025a) are not contradicted. Within this regime the dissociation is clean—the score’s failure mode characterized, the transfer asymmetry open—and adds an oracle-graded controlled cell to the elicitation-vs-expansion debate (Yue et al., 2025; Chu et al., 2025).

5 Interfaces Are Cheap, Knowledge Is Not

An installed model that cannot be addressed.

The dense-SFT model of §4 knows the post-edit response (0.667/0.680 given the edited description) but cannot apply an action: handed the original structure plus “add braces to story 3,” it drops to 0.513/0.533—a −0.15-0.15 interface gap on both tiers (Fig. 7, appendix). Installed, but not wired to the state++action interface.

Scores suffice to wire it.

Action-format GRPO—prompts are (state, random-story action) pairs, reward is the oracle’s score of the predicted post-action ranking—closes the gap exactly: tier-2 act 0.533→0.6870.533\to 0.687 vs. desc 0.687 (discordant 15:15, p=1.0p{=}1.0; Tables 5, 7), tier-1 0.76 vs. 0.73, with the forward and post-intervention axes at parity. This matches §4’s decomposition: the interface task starts half-right, so sampled behavior is rich in successes for selection to amplify (the transfer asymmetry of §4 notwithstanding).

But routing is not RL-specific: the dense control.

If wiring only takes training on the interface, dense supervision should do it too—and it does, plus more: SFT on the same action distribution (4k oracle-labeled pairs) closes the gap just as completely (tier-2 act 0.533→0.7600.533\to\mathbf{0.760}, p=6×10−7p=6\times 10^{-7}; own act−-desc gap n.s.) at zero knowledge tax (forward 0.740 vs. 0.747). On tier-1 it beats the RL route: post-intervention +0.140+0.140 (discordant 26:5, p=2×10−4p=2\times 10^{-4}), reaching 0.867—the paper’s highest post-intervention score—with act +0.087+0.087 (p=0.015p=0.015, secondary) trending the same way.

The dissociation, sharpened.

Wiring an interface is cheap: either use of the oracle buys it. Installing knowledge is expensive: only dense answers buy it, at any score budget we tested—and they install additional knowledge while wiring. In this regime, scores sufficed for routing and for nothing else we could measure—a narrow role that dense supervision fills at least as well wherever answers can be demonstrated. (Practically, pure SFT yields the best all-around model—action-SFT, post-intervention 0.867; the §6 rows belong to the assembled final checkpoint.)

The thinking channel: no measurable benefit, a possible cost.

Three pre-specified tier-2 contrasts (Appendix E) find no benefit from an explicit reasoning channel: repairing the channel that direct-answer SFT breaks costs knowledge (−0.073-0.073, p=0.013p{=}0.013, the only significant effect), thinking-on buys nothing, and think-RL vs. matched-compute nothink-RL is a tie favoring not thinking. Where the bottleneck is missing knowledge, deliberation cannot substitute for installation (Lightman et al., 2024).

6 Ceilings: Frontier, Specialist, and the Data-Precision Frontier

The frontier model we test sits near a 30-line formula.

Under a controlled API protocol (Appendix C), Claude Opus 4.8 localizes at 0.633/0.500 (tier-1/2). Against the first-order formula of §2.3 its lead is at most +0.10+0.10 (tier-1 forward, p=10−4p=10^{-4}) and +0.073+0.073 (tier-2 post-intervention, p=0.013p=0.013, secondary), n.s. on the other two cells—within a hair of thirty lines of physics, once surface cues are killed.

In-context examples do not install it.

The comparison is asymmetric—our model saw 4k oracle-labeled structures, the frontier model none. The in-context control narrows it: with 32 oracle-labeled worked examples Opus does not improve (tier-2 0.500→0.4330.500\to 0.433, p=0.087p=0.087; statistically still at the formula, p=0.86p{=}0.86, Table 6), while the trained 8B exceeds this 32-shot frontier by +0.300+0.300 (p<10−4p<10^{-4}; Fig. 6, appendix). In this design, in-context adaptation did not install what weight updates did (many-shot and tool use untested; Limitations).

A specialist baseline at parity.

A per-story GNN reading structured graph input—numeric sections, bracing topology, damage, load shape as features—trains on the same distribution and evaluates on the same instance streams. On tier-2 it matches our final text-reading model (0.733/0.733 forward, 0.680/0.680 post-intervention; discordants in Table 5); on fresh streams the pooled difference is bounded within ±0.06\pm 0.06 (n=1200n{=}1200, n.s., point estimate toward the LLM; Table 8). On tier-1 the LLM leads (0.84 vs. 0.82 forward; +0.100+0.100 post-int, p=0.058p=0.058). When the testbed gained its load-shape parameter, the GNN was blind until hand-rewired; the LLM read the change from a sentence.

The 0.73–0.78 convergence is a data-precision frontier.

Six learners with different inductive biases (0.733–0.780; Appendix F) converge on the same tier-2 band with no significant pairwise difference. The margin structure explains why (Fig. 5): 34% of tier-2 instances have a top-2 drift margin under 10%, so ±5%\pm 5\% per-story error caps top-1 at 0.83 and ±8%\pm 8\% at 0.78—bracketing the band. The band is a data-precision frontier, not a task ceiling: the task is noiseless, and RL’s consolidation moves within the wall without crossing it.

What moves the frontier—and what does not.

The data-efficiency curve (Fig. 5) locates the binding constraint: tier-1 saturates by n=1n=1k; tier-2 crawls (+0.02+0.02 at the last doubling)—while one difficulty-matched second round buys +0.09+0.09, worth three doublings. What is scarce is information near the decision boundary—curriculum beats volume.

7 Related Work

World models in language models. Probing shows sequence models can carry structured internal state (Li et al., 2023; Nanda et al., 2023; Kim and Schuster, 2023); audits show good prediction can coexist with a poor model of the generating process (Vafa et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024; Vafa et al., 2025)—they observe; we intervene. Physics-of-LMs (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2023) manipulates data properties; we manipulate the objective’s answer form, freezing the data. Supervision-content manipulations exist—traces with answers fixed (Bhambri et al., 2026), formats in logic tuning (Zhou et al., 2025)—without byte-identical inputs or counterfactual grading. Prakash et al. (2024) argue fine-tuning enhances existing mechanisms; our base starts at guessing, our placebo stays flat.

Limits of verifier-scored RL. Whether RLVR expands or merely elicits capability is contested (Yue et al., 2025; Chu et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025a; Shao et al., 2024; DeepSeek-AI, 2025); curation methods now assume RL needs the right SFT seed—the premise we measure (Yao et al., 2026). We contribute an oracle-graded controlled cell—one verifier, one start, uses dissociated—and a positive characterization: scores route; dense answers dominate (Uesato et al., 2022; Lightman et al., 2024).

LLMs for structural engineering. Zero-shot translator-plus-solver systems and spatial-physics benchmarks exist (Liang et al., 2025; Siedler, 2025)—the LLM translates while a hardcoded solver computes. Hage and Buehler (2026) RL-tunes a compact LLM on scalar beam statics (24 instances, uncontrolled)—consistent with our elicitation-regime account (§4). Ours is, to our knowledge, the first LLM trained on spatial (per-story) structural response, and the first controlled study of one.

8 Conclusion

The OraclePhys framework turns “what did training teach?” into a controlled variable—structural mechanics as a model organism. The label’s answer form determines what fine-tuning teaches; within the recipes tested, only written or score-filtered answers teach—advantage-weighted scores route.

Limitations

One scale, one recipe, synthetic domains. All results are 8B + LoRA, with GRPO at ≤\leq800 steps and group sizes up to 50; full-parameter training and prolonged-RL regimes (Liu et al., 2025a) remain open, and our negative claims are scoped accordingly (§4). Both testbeds are synthetic text over solvable physics, and heat conduction mirrors frames structurally: the replication evidences recipe robustness, not domain generality.

Behavioral claims only. “Installs a forward model” is operationalized behaviorally; linear probes do not adjudicate here (§2.1: they decode equally from every arm, including the behaviorally inert O, at the surface baseline) (Hewitt and Liang, 2019). We make no mechanistic claim; probing during generation is an open direction.

Evaluation scope. Post-edit structures belong to a family seen in training (the out-of-format evidence is the action interface). All evaluation axes are ordinal, so magnitude-trained arms (A/K/V) may install value models these axes do not credit—“installs less” means “on these axes”; a value-prediction axis (P should fail, V lead) is a natural extension.

One template; one in-context control. Descriptions instantiate a single fixed template—the price of byte-identical control; a paraphrased evaluation surface survives (Table 9). The frontier comparison is one model, one kk, text-only; many-shot (Agarwal et al., 2024) and tool use are untested—a tool-augmented model would likely solve the task, but what the tool knows is not what the weights carry.

Statistical scope. Gate arms carry three seeds; the control-suite arms (K/V/G/S) are single runs, to be read against the gate arms’ spread (±0.06{\pm}0.06); both decisive GRPO cells carry three seeds (§4). “Statistically indistinguishable” reports a failure to reject except where a TOST-style bound is given (Table 8).

Ethics Statement

OraclePhys is fully synthetic: all structures are procedurally generated; no human subjects, annotators, or personal data are involved anywhere. The testbed and any released checkpoints are research artifacts for studying training objectives and must not be used for real structural design, assessment, or code compliance: the FE oracle implements a simplified 2-D linear model that does not represent engineering practice. One hazard is specific to the data release: the OraclePhys-30K S partition carries deliberately shuffled (false) physics labels—it exists as a placebo control and must never be used as training supervision outside that role; its datasheet flags every affected file. The release ships under a research license with this intended-use statement attached, alongside the licenses of the assets it builds on (OpenSees, Qwen3, Llama-3.1, subject to their respective terms).

Appendix A Reproducibility

All instance streams are deterministic, so every run answers the same questions; every results file stores per-instance correctness arrays; and every number in the paper regenerates from the archived result files with a single script, with all comparisons run as exact McNemar tests (McNemar, 1947) with paired bootstrap CIs. Under greedy decoding, re-running a bench reproduces aggregates exactly. Code, result files, figure scripts, and the OraclePhys-30K supervision suite will be released, together with the evaluation streams exported as a static, FE-free benchmark (Appendix B): prompt text plus oracle truths per instance, surface-formula reference rows recomputed on the exported streams, and a SHA-256 over all truths as integrity fingerprints—external models can be scored, and paired against every model reported here, without installing the FE stack.

Appendix B Testbed details

Population and splits. Problems specify geometry (bays, stories, spans, story heights), constraints (forbidden brace cells), and the lateral load (total base shear; vertical profile Fx​(s)∝sαF_{x}(s)\propto s^{\alpha}). Training problems have 3–4 stories; the OOD pool has 5–6 stories under held-out geometry. Designs assign per-story column/beam sections from a discrete catalog, a connection type (pinned or moment), braced cells, and damage events.

Tier-1 sampler. Follows common design practice: near-monotone column profiles, code-style bracing layouts, isolated damage—regularities a surface reader can exploit (bag-of-words classifies the governing story at 0.63; geometry-only features 0.39; chance 0.18).

Tier-2 hardening. Three independent randomizations compose: (i) jittered column profiles—a bounded random walk over the section catalog replaces monotone profiles; (ii) composed weakening events—weak, twin, scatter, cutoff stack by independent coin flips (zero to four per structure), placing braces and damage so that no single event determines the answer; (iii) load-shape pool—α∈{0.7,1.0,1.4,2.0}\alpha\in\{0.7,1.0,1.4,2.0\}, written into the prompt. Verification: the bag-of-words probe falls to 0.26 (chance 0.18), geometry-only to 0.38, and the structured-feature probe from 0.76 to 0.57; ranking-target variants fall equally (rank-top-1 0.57→0.330.57\to 0.33).

The first-order formula. Story shear Vs=∑k≥sFkV_{s}=\sum_{k\geq s}F_{k} divided by a story-stiffness proxy aggregated from column sections (with a connection-type factor), brace areas, and damage multipliers; stories are ranked by Vs/KsV_{s}/K_{s}. It reads numeric section and brace properties from the design object directly—information strictly more direct than the prompt text—and scores 0.53/0.47 (tier-1) and 0.45/0.47 (tier-2) localization/post-intervention.

Heat-conduction isomorph. 2-D steady-state conduction on a grid with per-row materials from a conductivity catalog, high-conductivity cooling cells, near-insulating defects, and configurable heat-sink boundaries; the target is the per-row peak-temperature ranking. The mapping is: rows ↔\leftrightarrow stories; material catalog ↔\leftrightarrow section catalog; cooling cells ↔\leftrightarrow braces; insulating defects ↔\leftrightarrow damage; sink configuration ↔\leftrightarrow boundary conditions; source-shape exponent ↔\leftrightarrow load shape. Its audit: the 1-D two-sink ladder formula reaches 0.53 localization but only 0.21 post-intervention (2-D rerouting is invisible to it); prior 0.25; feature MLP 0.46.

Released benchmark. The four description axes of both tiers are exported as self-contained JSON (frames_tier{1,2}.json), with the heat-domain export, the 2-shot calibration prompts, and per-tier fingerprints shipped alongside: 150 instances per axis (80 for extrapolation), each carrying the exact prompt text and the oracle truths (governing story; full ranking where defined), so external models are scored with a pure-numpy parser and no FE dependency. Every instance asks the same ranking question: the readout instrument is held fixed while the training-side objective varies—scalar- or boolean-form questions are deliberately absent from the evaluation (a value-readout axis is the designed extension noted in the Limitations section). Two integrity anchors ship inside each file: the surface-formula reference row recomputed on the exported stream must match the paper’s fingerprints (0.5333/0.4733 on tier 1), and a SHA-256 over all truths pins the instance set. The invariance and action streams, which require paired or counterfactual FE calls, regenerate deterministically from the released code. Because per-instance correctness arrays for every model reported here are also released, an external model can be compared against any row of this paper by exact McNemar test without re-running our models.

Appendix C Training details

Supervised arms. Qwen3-8B (and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for the family replication) with LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) r=32r{=}32, α=64\alpha{=}64, dropout 0.05; lr 10−410^{-4}; 3 epochs; cutoff 2048; batch 2 ×\times 4 accumulation; seed 42 (plus 43/44 for the frames staircase). The three gate arms share byte-identical structure text (asserted at build time with a token-level leakage audit) and differ only in the question–answer suffix. The round-2 dense stage resumes the tier-1 P adapter on hardened-pool labels; the action-SFT control resumes the round-2 adapter on 4k oracle-labeled (state, action) →\to ranking pairs drawn from the same distribution as the action-GRPO pool (uniform random story; connection-preserving brace edit).

GRPO. TRL implementation with the Dr. GRPO loss (Liu et al., 2025b) (loss_type=dr_grpo, no length normalization) and scale_rewards=False (advantages not divided by group std); group size g=8g{=}8; lr 10−610^{-6}; temperature 1.0; no KL anchor (β=0\beta{=}0); completion cap 512 tokens (768 with thinking); 400–800 steps; per-device batch 1 with 8-step accumulation on 7–8 RTX 3090s. Reward: 0.6⋅(ρSpearman+1)/2+0.4⋅𝟏​[top-1 correct]0.6\cdot(\rho_{\text{Spearman}}+1)/2+0.4\cdot\mathbf{1}[\text{top-1 correct}], with unparseable completions floored at −0.5-0.5. Budgets per protocol: the dense round trains ∼1.4{\sim}1.4k optimizer steps at lr 10−410^{-4}; GRPO trains 400–800 steps at lr 10−610^{-6} with 8 rollouts per prompt; the think-RL/nothink-RL contrast matches Y’s steps and configuration to X exactly. Total compute across all training runs, seeds, and evaluations in the paper is on the order of 300 RTX-3090 GPU-hours; frontier-model calls total ∼600{\sim}600 API requests. Round-1 diagnostics recorded the within-group reward-std collapse (0.122→0.0490.122\to 0.049) that motivated the difficulty-filtered round-2. Variants used in §4–5: difficulty filtering (train only on prompts whose greedy answer scores below a threshold), the action-format pool, and the best-practice cell (g=50g{=}50, five-way data parallel, filter threshold 0.9).

Frontier protocol. API models are queried one instance per call with responses disk-cached; Claude Opus 4.8 with adaptive thinking enabled and provider-default decoding; the 32-shot condition prepends worked train-split examples with oracle answers under prompt caching; outputs are parsed by the shared parser and a parse failure scores as a miss. The verification row of §2.4 is recomputed on the identical stream post hoc.

OraclePhys-30K composition. Seven answer-form arms ×\times 3,760 byte-identical training rows (26,320), plus action-interface supervision (∼4{\sim}4k pairs) and the hardened second-round curriculum (§4); every label except the S placebo is written programmatically from the oracle’s solution.

Arm and checkpoint glossary. Training arms: P ranking; A peak scalar; O compliance boolean; K pointwise scalar; V value vector; G governing story only; S shuffled placebo. Checkpoints: SFT-hard = P + dense hardened round; RFT = P + filtered self-distillation; Y = SFT-hard + no-think GRPO; X = think-bridge + GRPO pipeline; BP-GRPO = SFT-hard + g=50g{=}50 filtered GRPO; final = SFT-hard + action-GRPO (the RL-routed assembly); action-SFT = SFT-hard + action-label SFT (the pure-supervised assembly, deployed flagship).

An example instance (tier-1 forward stream, verbatim).

A 3-bay, 5-story steel frame (26 ft bays, 13 ft story height) under lateral seismic load (total base shear 74 kip, increasing with height).
- beam (all floors): W21x68
- columns by story: story 1: W12x53; story 2: W12x53; story 3: W8x24; story 4: W12x53; story 5: W12x53
- beam-column connections: moment (rigid joints)
- braced cells: story 1: bays [1, 2, 3]; story 2: bays [1, 2, 3]; story 3: bays [1, 3]; story 4: bays [1, 2, 3]
Rank ALL 5 stories from LARGEST to SMALLEST inter-story drift ratio (story 1 = bottom, story 5 = top). Respond with JSON only: {"ranking": [story numbers, largest-drift first]}.

Oracle answer: ranking [5,3,2,4,1][5,3,2,4,1], governing story 5: the only unbraced story sits at the top of a height-weighted load, yet story 3’s section cut plus missing brace nearly overtake it—the ranking requires weighing both effects, and no single sentence carries the answer. Descriptions are templated with randomized structure; surface-cue exploitability is audited and hardened in tier-2 (§2.3).

Thinking bridge. 4k programmatic rationales ("evidence lines →\to verdict →\to answer," generated from structure features and FE ground truth; ∼170{\sim}170 tokens) fine-tuned on the dense-SFT model restore think-mode termination (zero clipping from 100%). X continues this checkpoint with GRPO under thinking; Y applies matched-compute GRPO to the same parent without thinking.

Appendix D Alternative-explanation sweep for §4

Reward design. The reward (Appendix C) is graded, not binary: 60% continuous full-profile rank correlation plus 40% explicit localization credit, with a parse floor that preserves gradient toward well-formed answers. The two densifications a critic would propose—reward the profile shape; reward localization directly—are both already present. What no scalar reward can add is the label’s content itself (§4).

Optimizer health. Over GRPO training the reward climbs 0.80→0.930.80\to 0.93 and in-pool localization 0.74→0.880.74\to 0.88 while OOD localization moves +0.01+0.01: optimization succeeds at its stated objective; the objective is satisfiable without transferable physics. The headroom-matched relaunch reproduces the pattern from the lower start: reward 0.62→0.690.62\to 0.69, in-pool localization 0.41→0.550.41\to 0.55 (first- vs. last-40-step means), OOD +0.013+0.013.

Exploration. The round-2 recipe trains exclusively on unsolved prompts (greedy-score filtering) with g=8g{=}8 samples at temperature 1.0; OOD localization moves 0.667→0.6870.667\to 0.687 (p=0.15p{=}0.15 vs. the dense control’s 0.747).

Capacity. The identical LoRA configuration absorbs +0.09+0.09 to +0.14+0.14 on every axis when the oracle writes answers (Table 1), so parametric capacity does not bind.

Appendix E Thinking-channel details (§5)

Direct-answer SFT leaves the model unable to use its thinking mode: asked to reason before answering, 100% of generations hit the token limit without closing the think block. The rationale bridge is 4k automatically generated chains of the form “evidence lines →\to verdict →\to answer”—evidence lines read off structure features (sections, bracing, damage, load shape), the verdict names the governing story, the answer repeats the JSON ranking—fine-tuned on top of the dense-SFT checkpoint with the same LoRA configuration. After the bridge, thinking terminates in ∼170{\sim}170 tokens with zero clipping, and length stays stable (∼172{\sim}172 tokens) throughout subsequent RL, so the on/off contrast in §5 runs on identical weights with a functioning channel in both conditions.

The three §5 contrasts (n=150n{=}150, exact McNemar): (i) bridge cost: thinking off, the bridged model scores 0.673 vs. its 0.747 parent (−0.073-0.073, discordant 3:14, p=0.013p{=}0.013); (ii) thinking on: forward +0.033+0.033 (p=0.33p{=}0.33), post-intervention −0.013-0.013 (p=0.81p{=}0.81); (iii) think-RL vs. nothink-RL from the same SFT-hard ancestor (X via the bridge, Y directly; the gap is commensurate with the bridge tax of (i)): 0.707 vs. 0.760, 95% CI [−0.133,+0.027][-0.133,+0.027], p=0.27p{=}0.27, the point estimate favoring not thinking. RL preserves the channel (thinking length stable throughout); it never pays for itself.
